answer.label: Not Gautama Buddha — a modern saying
answer.authorName: A. J. Muste, adapted by Wayne Dyer & Thich Nhat Hanh
answer.sourceLine: This is a fake Buddha quote ↗ — it appears in no Buddhist scripture. The memorable formula is American pacifist A. J. Muste’s credo “There is no way to peace, peace is the way.” Self-help writer Wayne Dyer recast it as “There is no way to happiness; happiness is the way” in Pulling Your Own Strings (1978), and Thich Nhat Hanh later popularized a happiness–peace–enlightenment version.

source.excerpt: There is no way to happiness; happiness is the way.
trail: No Buddhist canonical text contains this line; Fake Buddha Quotes ↗ identifies it as a genuine fake Buddha quote.
The underlying formula is A. J. Muste’s pacifist credo “There is no way to peace, peace is the way,” the subject of the scholarly review “There Is No Way to Peace, Peace Is the Way” ↗.

Per Fake Buddha Quotes, the exact “happiness” wording appears in Wayne Dyer’s Pulling Your Own Strings (1978), and Thich Nhat Hanh expanded it into a happiness–peace–enlightenment triad in The Art of Mindful Living (1992).
source.excerptNote: Thich Nhat Hanh’s expanded form runs: “There is no way to happiness, happiness is the way. There is no way to peace, peace is the way. There is no way to enlightenment, enlightenment is the way.”

source.rightsHolder: Estate of Wayne W. Dyer / publishers of Wayne Dyer and Thich Nhat Hanh; A. J. Muste’s works and estate for the “peace” original
source.rightsNote: This is a modern 20th-century saying, not an ancient text. A. J. Muste’s original “peace” credo dates to c. 1967, and the exact “happiness” wording is documented in Wayne Dyer’s Pulling Your Own Strings (1978) and Thich Nhat Hanh’s The Art of Mindful Living (1992) — all published after 1931 and therefore in copyright. There is no public-domain Buddhist source, because the Buddha did not say it.

author.name: A. J. Muste
author.heading: About A. J. Muste
author.bio: Abraham Johannes Muste was a Dutch-born American clergyman who moved from Calvinist preaching to militant labor organizing and finally to radical Christian pacifism, becoming one of the 20th century’s leading nonviolence advocates. His credo — “There is no way to peace, peace is the way” — became the template later writers adapted to happiness, enlightenment and other ideals. It was never a saying of the Buddha.

misattribution.heading: How it got pinned on the Buddha
misattribution.intro: Short, serene and about happiness, this line is a magnet for the Buddha’s name — but it is a 20th-century Western coinage with a documented paper trail.

items.why: The sentence appears in no Buddhist canon or sutra. Fake Buddha Quotes ↗ classifies it as a genuine fake Buddha quote.
The pacifist minister’s credo “There is no way to peace, peace is the way” is the template everything else riffs on — see the OSU scholarly review ↗ named for it.

Wayne Dyer used the happiness version in Pulling Your Own Strings (1978) without crediting anyone, and Thich Nhat Hanh spread it further in The Art of Mindful Living (1992) — which is why it is often credited to him ↗ too.

misattribution.truthLine: The Buddha never said it: it is A. J. Muste’s “peace is the way” credo, recast for happiness by Wayne Dyer and Thich Nhat Hanh ↗.

context.heading: Why the mix-up sticks
lead: The phrase belongs to a family of “there is no way to X; X is the way” aphorisms that all descend from A. J. Muste’s pacifism. Because Thich Nhat Hanh — a Buddhist monk — used and expanded it, the leap from “a Buddhist teacher said it” to “the Buddha said it” was an easy one for meme-makers to make.
context.pull: Muste’s peace credo, recast for happiness — not a sutra.
